A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REKD study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material moved from v1 Appendix C to v2 Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original BERT and ViT experiments on IMDB and CIFAR 10/100, including predictive results, hyperparameter studies, and rationale examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CIFAR-10 ablation results and an IMDB teacher/student case study.

M1.justification: The proposed select-predict architecture, Straight-Through Gumbel-Softmax sampling, rationale and prediction distillation losses, combined objective, and shared temperature schedule are unchanged. Newly evaluated component variants are ablations, not revisions to REKD.

E1.justification: Both versions use IMDB sentiment classification, CIFAR-10 classification, and CIFAR-100 with 20 coarse classes. The added ablations and IMDB example remain within these existing datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix C adds self-distillation, rationale-only distillation, and prediction-only distillation as internal comparators on CIFAR-10. The main CLS/RE comparisons remain unchanged. KD-only with alpha=0 was already evaluated in v1; its newly reported accuracy is not a newly introduced comparator.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated role of the 5,000-sample IMDB holdout from testing to development, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Appendix C adds controlled self-distillation and component-removal comparisons, explicitly retaining other REKD settings. Existing training budgets, preprocessing, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds central mechanism tests separating teacher knowledge from supervision-related optimization benefits and rationale distillation from prediction distillation. It also augments the existing alpha=0 check with accuracy results and adds an IMDB failure/correction example in Figure 1. These substantially extend the earlier tuning and sanity-check analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten runs with seeds 2026–2035 and report standard deviations in Tables 1–3. Existing appendix run-count exceptions are retained. The new ablations continue the appendix practice of reporting averages, without introducing a new uncertainty estimator, significance test, or increased run count.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores and earlier tuning results are unchanged, but v2 Tables 4–6 add substantive component-level findings. For ViT Tiny on CIFAR-10, newly reported accuracies are 0.928 for KD-only, 0.820 for self-distillation, 0.930 for rationale-only, and 0.650 for prediction-only, alongside retained REKD accuracy 0.936. Figure 1 adds a qualitative error-correction result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, annealing formula, and Appendix B gradient derivation are retained. Moving the predictor equation inline and renumbering subsequent equations do not change their mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: REKD addresses difficult joint rationale learning through architecture-agnostic distillation and synchronized annealing, improving lightweight students on the same language and vision tasks.

C2.justification: New Section 6 discusses covert communication through selections, difficulty validating rationale quality, human usability studies, and shared-input/tokenization requirements across architectures. It also asserts a regularizing benefit against covert channels. Appendix C newly attributes gains mainly to teacher knowledge and rationale distillation. The earlier proposed future direction of dynamically weighting RE and KD is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a REKD code-repository link in the abstract. Existing model and dataset identifiers, hardware information, optimizer settings, and hyperparameters are retained, with experimental details moved from Appendix C to Appendix D.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wäldchen et al. (2024) and Liu et al. (2025) to contextualize covert-channel and spurious-correlation risks in rationalization. The existing related-work comparisons and novelty positioning are otherwise substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, updates affiliations and publication information, and adds acknowledgements. It separates limitations/discussion from the conclusion and moves the KD-only discussion into a dedicated ablation appendix. Most existing prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the IMDB comparison figure and three ablation tables. Existing diagrams, plots, and result tables are retained with localized relocation and caption changes. The earlier rationale-example figure is reformatted, including removal of the displayed CLS token, rather than replaced by new examples.

improvement.justification: The new ablations strengthen evidence about the source of REKD's gains, while the limitations discussion, illustrative example, and code-access information improve clarity and assessability. The gains are bounded: the new controls cover CIFAR-10 only and report means without dispersion, while the new assertion that distillation suppresses covert communication is not directly tested. Overall, v2 offers a useful but limited improvement over the retained main evidence.
